assisted.text: Nice work exploring this topic with some guidance. You can use Practice whenever you'd like to try the activities on your own.

explored.text: That's the end of this topic. You can revisit anything you skipped or want to practice, or choose another topic.

references.action: Replay Welcome, choose a topic, and use Practice to revisit activities. Help demonstrates; Skip leaves an activity for later.
references.caution: These are Learn Omarchy course controls, not default Omarchy shortcuts. Introduced content is not proof of hands-on practice.

references.action: Capture Keys sends input to the coach; Release Keys gives input to desktop apps. Return to Capture Keys to resume guided shortcuts.
references.caution: Released shortcuts affect your real desktop. Course-owned-window protections do not apply to everyday shortcuts.

lessons.title: Welcome to Omarchy
lessons.description: Meet your coach and discover how to make this desktop your own. Replay the welcome anytime.

references.action: The bar provides workspaces, clock and system controls. Super is the Windows-logo key, or Command on a Mac keyboard.
Each workspace holds its own windows. The active marker can be an icon rather than a number; switching keeps windows open.
Switch to workspace two without moving or closing its windows.
Switch to workspace one.
Click the clock for the calendar. Hover for quick tools such as reminders and recording; weather appears when enabled.
Select network, Bluetooth, audio or power indicators to inspect controls. Available indicators depend on hardware and bar settings.
Open the Omarchy menu for apps, settings and system tools.
Click the Omarchy icon to open the same menu without a keyboard shortcut.

wrapUp.text: Nice work, that's the tour. You've explored the desktop bar, switched workspaces, and opened the Omarchy menu.

lessons.title: Omarchy tour
lessons.description: Get oriented with the desktop bar, try switching workspaces, then open the Omarchy menu.

steps.instruction: Let's start with the highlighted desktop bar. It gives you quick access to workspaces, the clock, and system controls. You'll use the Super key for many of Omarchy's keyboard shortcuts. On a Mac keyboard, that's Command. On a Windows keyboard, it's the Windows-logo key. When I say "hold Super," that's the key to use.
steps.detail: Follow the highlighted area if your bar is in a different position. Read along or listen, then press Enter to continue. Help can demonstrate shortcuts when you need it.

steps.instruction: These are your workspaces: separate desktops for different tasks. The active workspace has a marker in the bar, which may replace its number with an icon. Switching workspaces keeps your windows open.
steps.detail: Follow the highlighted area. Choose Next or press Enter when you're ready to continue.

steps.practicePrompt: Switch to workspace two. Leave your windows open.
steps.note: Your windows stay open when you switch workspaces.
steps.instruction: Hold Super and tap 2 on the top row. Then release both keys.
steps.detail: Switching workspaces doesn't close or move your windows. Workspace two may already have windows in it. If you're already there, we'll move on to switching to workspace one.
steps.completionMessage: You're on workspace two. Look for the active marker at workspace two's position in the bar. It may be an icon instead of a number. Your other windows are still on their own workspaces.

steps.practicePrompt: Return to workspace one.
steps.instruction: Now hold Super and tap 1 on the top row. Then release both keys. You're heading to workspace one.
steps.detail: If you started on workspace one, this brings you back. If you started elsewhere, it takes you to workspace one instead. Nothing is closed or moved.
steps.completionMessage: You're on workspace one. You can use the same shortcut whenever you want to switch workspaces. Let's continue along the bar.

steps.instruction: Here's the date and time, with weather alongside it if enabled. The clock opens a calendar. Hovering over this area can also reveal quick tools, including reminders and screen recording.
steps.detail: Follow the highlighted area. Choose Next or press Enter when you're ready to continue.

steps.instruction: These indicators show system status, including network, Bluetooth, sound, and power. Select an indicator to open its controls. What you see depends on your hardware and bar settings.
steps.detail: Follow the highlighted area. Choose Next or press Enter when you're ready to continue.

steps.practicePrompt: Open the Omarchy menu.
steps.instruction: Let's try another shortcut. Hold Super and tap Space to open the Omarchy menu.
steps.detail: The Omarchy menu brings together apps, settings, and system tools. Super and Space opens it whenever you need it.
steps.completionMessage: That's the Omarchy menu in the center of your screen. It brings together apps, settings, and system tools. Super and Space opens it whenever you need it.

steps.instruction: You can also click this icon in the desktop bar to open the same menu, with apps, settings, and other resources. Use whichever way is more convenient.
steps.detail: The previous menu is closed so you can see the icon clearly. This is the mouse alternative to Super and Space; you don't need to click it to finish the tour.

references.action: Open the Omarchy menu for apps, settings and system tools.
Open Apps to search launchable applications, not every installed package. Alt is Option on a Mac keyboard.
Open Apps, type Terminal or Ghostty, select the installed terminal and press Enter. In the COURSE, choose Start search first, then close the newly opened terminal to finish.
references.caution: Escape clears typed search text; press again to close, or once if empty. Check the focused window before closing anything.

references.action: Close the focused window.
references.caution: Save work first. This is not limited to the terminal opened for practice.

references.action: Open the shortcut guide and type to filter bindings.
references.caution: Enter or clicking a result runs that shortcut, potentially closing a window or locking the screen. Read without activating unfamiliar results.

wrapUp.text: That wraps up menus and apps. You have a starting point for finding commands, opening apps, and looking up shortcuts.

lessons.title: Menus and apps
lessons.description: Find commands, installed apps, and the built-in shortcut guide.

steps.practicePrompt: Open the main Omarchy menu.
steps.instruction: Press Super and Space to open the Omarchy menu. If you tried this on the tour, use it as a quick refresher or choose Skip.
steps.detail: This menu is a useful starting point for apps, settings, and system tools.
steps.completionMessage: The Omarchy menu is open. It brings together apps, settings, and system tools. The course will close it when you continue.

steps.practicePrompt: Open the Apps menu.
steps.instruction: Now for your apps. Alt is the Option key on a Mac keyboard. Hold Super and Alt, then tap Space to open the Apps menu.
steps.detail: The Apps menu lists launchable apps, not every installed package. The next exercise gives you control so you can search for and launch an app yourself.
steps.completionMessage: The Apps menu is open. The next exercise lets you search for and launch an app yourself.

steps.note: I'll stay here while you use the Apps menu; your existing windows are left alone.
steps.instruction: Choose Start search. Open the Apps menu with Super, Alt, and Space. Search for Terminal or Ghostty, then press Enter. Close the new terminal with Super and W to finish.
steps.detail: Start search gives your keyboard to the desktop while the coach stays here. Search for the terminal installed on your system. Closing the new terminal finishes automatically; no separate exercise window opens.
steps.completionMessage: You opened the menu, launched a new terminal, and closed that window. Searching the Apps menu is a useful way to find an app when you don't know its shortcut.

steps.practicePrompt: Open the shortcut guide. Read only: pressing Enter or clicking a result runs that shortcut.
steps.instruction: Need to look up a shortcut? Press Super and K to open the shortcut guide. Read only for this lesson: pressing Enter or clicking a result runs that shortcut, which could close windows or lock your screen.
steps.detail: The guide can filter shortcuts as you type. For now, read the visible key combinations without activating a result.
steps.note: Read only: Enter or clicking a result runs the shortcut, not a help page.
steps.completionMessage: The shortcut guide is open. It lists Omarchy shortcuts and can filter them as you type. Looking is enough for this lesson.

references.action: Open a terminal for commands. Return is the Enter key on most keyboards.
Close the focused window.
references.caution: Save work and verify focus first; any focused app can close, not only a practice terminal or file manager.

references.action: Launch the configured browser. Browser settings determine whether a new window opens.
Open the file manager to browse folders and documents.

wrapUp.text: Nicely done. You've practiced opening everyday apps and closing the windows you no longer need.

lessons.title: Everyday apps
lessons.description: Launch the terminal, browser, and file manager, and learn to close what you open.

steps.practicePrompt: Open a new terminal window.
steps.note: A terminal is a window where you can type commands.
steps.instruction: Press Super and Return to open a terminal. Return is the Enter key on most keyboards.
steps.detail: A terminal is a window where you can type commands. You won't need to enter commands in this activity. Omarchy fits the new window alongside your existing work.
steps.completionMessage: That's your terminal, one shortcut away from anywhere in Omarchy.

steps.practicePrompt: Close the terminal you just opened.
steps.note: Only the terminal opened for this activity will close.
steps.instruction: Now let's tidy up. Press Super and W to close that terminal.
steps.detail: Super and W closes the active window: the one receiving your input. Here it closes only the terminal you just opened.
steps.completionMessage: The practice terminal is closed. Super and Return opens one; Super and W closes the active window.

steps.practicePrompt: Open a new browser window.
steps.instruction: Let's get online. Hold Super and Shift, then press Return to open your browser.
steps.detail: This shortcut uses the browser you've configured in Omarchy. Browser settings can affect whether a new window opens.
steps.completionMessage: Your browser is ready. Super, Shift, and Return is the shortcut to remember.

steps.practicePrompt: Open the Files application.
steps.note: A file manager helps you browse folders and documents.
steps.instruction: Need your files? Hold Super and Shift, then press F to open the file manager.
steps.detail: The file manager opens in a new window, ready for browsing, drag and drop, or a quick search.
steps.completionMessage: The file manager is open. Use it to browse folders, find documents, and manage files.

steps.practicePrompt: Close the Files window opened by this lesson.
steps.note: Your other windows stay open.
steps.instruction: Same move again. Press Super and W to close the file manager.
steps.detail: This closes only the Files window you just opened, not another window on your desktop.
steps.completionMessage: The file manager is closed. You can keep the browser open or close it when you're finished with it.

references.action: Open a terminal. Tiling fits additional windows into the available workspace without overlap.
Toggle the split direction within the dwindle layout; repeat to toggle back.
references.caution: Needs tiled windows in dwindle. This does not switch workspace layouts or provide the same split behavior in floating, scrolling or custom layouts.

references.action: Cycle focus through windows on the active workspace. Focus determines which window receives keyboard input.
references.caution: Includes your existing windows, not just practice windows.

references.action: Toggle the focused window between floating and tiling. Repeat to return it to the tiled layout.
Resize horizontally by a 100-pixel step using physical keycode 21, immediately left of Backspace (normally equals on US keyboards).
references.caution: No Shift or Plus key is needed. Physical position, window size limits and the movable tiled edge determine the result.

references.action: Resize horizontally in the other direction by a 100-pixel step using physical keycode 20, two places left of Backspace (normally minus on US keyboards).
references.caution: These are physical keycodes, not character bindings. Tiled edges and size limits affect the result; reversing need not restore the exact size.

references.action: Resize height instead of width by a 100-pixel step.
references.caution: Use physical keycode 21, immediately left of Backspace, not a typed Plus character. Layout constraints still apply.

references.action: Resize height in the other direction by a 100-pixel step.
references.caution: Use physical keycode 20, two places left of Backspace. Layout constraints still apply.

references.action: Use a finer 25-pixel horizontal resize step. Add Shift for height instead of width.
references.caution: Use physical keycode 21, immediately left of Backspace. Size limits and tiled edges can prevent resizing.

references.action: Use a finer 25-pixel horizontal resize step in the other direction. Add Shift for height.
references.caution: Use physical keycode 20, two places left of Backspace. Size limits and tiled edges can prevent resizing.

references.action: Use a larger 300-pixel horizontal resize step. Add Shift for height instead of width.
references.caution: Use physical keycode 21, immediately left of Backspace. Size limits and tiled edges can prevent resizing.

references.action: Use a larger 300-pixel horizontal resize step in the other direction. Add Shift for height.
references.caution: Use physical keycode 20, two places left of Backspace. Size limits and tiled edges can prevent resizing.

references.action: Toggle fullscreen for the focused window; repeat to leave fullscreen.
Focus the neighboring window in the chosen direction: left, right, up or down.
Swap the focused window with the adjacent window in the chosen direction.
references.caution: Changes both windows' positions, including existing work. Check focus and the neighbor first.

references.action: Close the focused window; remaining tiles reclaim its space.
references.caution: Save work first. The shortcut can close any focused window.

wrapUp.text: Nice work. You've practiced arranging windows and switching your focus between them. Use the layout that suits your task.

lessons.title: Windows
lessons.description: Tile, split, resize, focus, float, and fullscreen practice windows.

steps.practicePrompt: Open a terminal to begin practicing window management.
steps.note: Tiling arranges your windows without overlap.
steps.instruction: Let's see how tiling works. Press Super and Return to open a terminal.
steps.detail: Tiling arranges windows without overlap. A single tiled window fills the available workspace; additional windows share that space.
steps.completionMessage: The terminal has joined your layout. Next, open another to see how the available space is shared.

steps.practicePrompt: Open a second terminal, keeping the first one open.
steps.instruction: Press Super and Return once more to open a second terminal.
steps.detail: Tiling means no overlapping and no manual arranging. Omarchy splits the space for you.
steps.completionMessage: There's your second practice terminal. Omarchy fits it around any windows you already had open.

steps.practicePrompt: Change the split between the two tiled practice terminals.
steps.note: Split changes require the dwindle layout and two tiled practice windows.
steps.instruction: Press Super and J to change how the two practice terminals share their space. A split is the dividing line between tiles: this shortcut changes its direction.
steps.detail: Watch the same two terminals change from side by side to stacked, or the reverse. This requires Omarchy's dwindle layout. If you use scrolling or another custom layout, choose Skip instead of changing your workspace settings.

help.label: Toggle the split for me
command: local target = hl.get_window("{tutorialWindow}"); local peer = hl.get_window("{peerWindow}"); assert(target and peer and target.address ~= peer.address and not target.floating and not peer.floating and target.fullscreen == 0 and peer.fullscreen == 0 and target.workspace.id == peer.workspace.id, "Practice windows are not ready"); hl.dispatch(hl.dsp.focus({ window = "{tutorialWindow}" })); local active = hl.get_active_window(); assert(active and active.address == target.address, "Practice window could not be focused"); hl.dispatch(hl.dsp.layout("togglesplit"))

steps.completionMessage: The two practice terminals now share the space in the other direction.

steps.practicePrompt: Toggle the practice terminals' split direction once more.
steps.note: This changes the split again, not the workspace's layout setting.
steps.instruction: Press Super and J again to toggle the dividing line back. Both terminals should stay tiled.
steps.detail: The same shortcut toggles in both directions. Only the two terminals from this lesson are used.

help.label: Toggle the split back for me
command: local target = hl.get_window("{tutorialWindow}"); local peer = hl.get_window("{peerWindow}"); assert(target and peer and target.address ~= peer.address and not target.floating and not peer.floating and target.fullscreen == 0 and peer.fullscreen == 0 and target.workspace.id == peer.workspace.id, "Practice windows are not ready"); hl.dispatch(hl.dsp.focus({ window = "{tutorialWindow}" })); local active = hl.get_active_window(); assert(active and active.address == target.address, "Practice window could not be focused"); hl.dispatch(hl.dsp.layout("togglesplit"))

steps.completionMessage: The practice terminals' split direction changed again. This is different from floating a window.

steps.practicePrompt: Switch keyboard focus to the other practice terminal.
steps.note: Focus means which window receives your keyboard input.
steps.instruction: Two windows, one keyboard. Press Alt and Tab to hop to the other terminal.
steps.detail: Focus means which window receives keyboard input. Alt and Tab switches windows; the active border helps you spot the change. This guided step selects your other practice terminal.
steps.completionMessage: The other terminal now receives your keyboard input. You can switch between windows without moving them.

steps.practicePrompt: Make the focused practice terminal float instead of staying tiled.
steps.note: Floating windows can sit above the tiled layout.
steps.instruction: Sometimes you want a window to float free. Press Super and T to toggle floating.
steps.detail: A floating window sits on top of the tiles and can be dragged around with Super and the mouse. Press Super and T again to tile it back.
steps.completionMessage: It's floating now. Handy for a calculator or a chat window you want to keep in view.

steps.practicePrompt: Change the width of the floating practice terminal.
steps.note: Use the key immediately left of Backspace, normally = on a US keyboard.
steps.instruction: With the practice terminal floating, hold Super and press the key immediately left of Backspace. On a US keyboard it is equals. This changes the window's width; you do not need Shift.
steps.detail: Omarchy uses the key's physical position rather than its printed symbol. This widens only the floating terminal. Window size limits may prevent a change; choose Skip if the terminal cannot resize.

help.label: Resize the practice terminal for me
command: hl.dispatch(hl.dsp.window.resize({ window = "{tutorialWindow}", x = 100, y = 0, relative = true }))

steps.completionMessage: The practice terminal changed size. Floating makes the width change easy to see.

steps.practicePrompt: Change the floating practice terminal's width in the other direction.
steps.note: Use the key two places left of Backspace, normally minus on a US keyboard.
steps.instruction: Now hold Super and press the key two places left of Backspace, normally minus. This resizes in the other direction. Adding Shift changes height instead of width.
steps.detail: The physical minus-position key is code 20. Alt makes a resize smaller, 25 pixels instead of 100; Control makes it larger, 300 pixels. Tiled resizing also depends on which shared edge can move. This exercise verifies a size change, not an exact restoration to the original size.

help.label: Resize the other way for me
command: hl.dispatch(hl.dsp.window.resize({ window = "{tutorialWindow}", x = -100, y = 0, relative = true }))

steps.completionMessage: The terminal changed size again. Width and height use the same two physical keys, with Shift selecting height.

steps.practicePrompt: Make the floating practice terminal fullscreen.
steps.note: Use the same shortcut again to leave fullscreen.
steps.instruction: Need to focus on one thing? Press Super and F for fullscreen.
steps.detail: Super+F toggles fullscreen. You'll press the same shortcut again in the next activity to get your desktop back.
steps.completionMessage: The terminal is fullscreen. Press the same shortcut in the next activity to leave fullscreen.

steps.practicePrompt: Take the practice terminal out of fullscreen.
steps.instruction: Press Super and F again to leave fullscreen.
steps.detail: The same shortcut gets you in and out, so you're never stuck.
steps.completionMessage: Fullscreen is off. You can return to the bar and your other windows.

steps.practicePrompt: Return the floating practice terminal to the tiled layout.
steps.instruction: Press Super and T to put that floating terminal back into the tiled layout.
steps.detail: Tiling fits the practice window around your existing work.
steps.completionMessage: Your terminal is tiled again. Omarchy manages its size and position alongside the other windows.

steps.practicePrompt: Focus the neighboring practice terminal using the directional window-focus shortcut.
steps.instruction: Super and an arrow focuses a neighboring window. Use the highlighted arrow to focus your other practice terminal.
steps.detail: The arrow follows the terminals' actual positions. Your existing windows are left unchanged.
steps.completionMessage: Your second terminal has focus. Directional shortcuts save you from cycling through every window.

steps.practicePrompt: Swap the positions of the two practice terminals using the directional swap shortcut.
steps.note: Only our two practice terminals will change positions.
steps.instruction: Add Shift to swap window positions. Hold Super and Shift, then press the highlighted arrow.
steps.detail: This normally swaps the active window with its neighbor. Here it exchanges only the two practice terminals.
steps.completionMessage: Your practice terminals traded places. Adding Shift changes directional focus into a window swap.

steps.practicePrompt: Close the focused practice terminal, leaving the other one open.
steps.instruction: Let's clean up. Press Super and W to close this window.
steps.detail: Closing a tiled window gives its space back to the others instantly.
steps.completionMessage: The first practice terminal is closed. The remaining windows can use the space it released.

steps.practicePrompt: Close the remaining practice terminal.
steps.instruction: And once more. Press Super and W to close the last terminal.
steps.detail: That's the whole loop: open, arrange, focus, close. All from the keyboard.
steps.completionMessage: Both practice terminals are closed. You've covered opening, arranging, switching between, and closing windows.

references.action: Switch to workspace one.
Open a terminal on the current workspace. Each workspace holds its own windows.
Switch to workspace two, leaving windows open on their own workspaces.
Return to the last workspace you visited.
Move the focused window to workspace two and follow it there. Also restores a visible, focused scratchpad window to that numbered workspace.
references.caution: Check focus first. A hidden scratchpad window is not the target; reveal it and select it before moving.

references.action: Switch to the next workspace.
Switch to the previous workspace.
Move the focused window to the scratchpad, a hidden workspace that can appear over your desktop.
references.caution: Verify which window has focus before stashing it.

references.action: Toggle scratchpad show/hide. Hidden scratchpad windows stay open; reveal and focus the intended window before restoring it.
Close the focused window.
references.caution: Save work and check focus first; the native shortcut is not restricted to a practice terminal.

wrapUp.text: That wraps up workspaces. You can keep different tasks on separate desktops and switch between them without closing your windows.

lessons.title: Workspaces
lessons.description: Jump between desktops, send windows where they belong, and stash things in the scratchpad.

steps.practicePrompt: Switch to workspace one to begin.
steps.instruction: First, let's start from workspace one. Press Super and 1.
steps.detail: If you're already on workspace one, this step takes care of itself.
steps.completionMessage: You're on workspace one. We'll use it as the starting point for this lesson.

steps.practicePrompt: Open a terminal on workspace one. You'll move it between workspaces.
steps.instruction: We'll need a window to move around. Press Super and Return to open a terminal.
steps.detail: Workspaces are separate desktops. Each one holds its own set of tiled windows.
steps.completionMessage: The practice terminal is open. Watch the workspace numbers as you move between desktops.

steps.practicePrompt: Switch to workspace two without moving the terminal.
steps.note: Your windows stay open when you switch workspaces.
steps.instruction: Press Super and 2 to visit workspace two.
steps.detail: Workspaces separate your tasks. A workspace may already contain windows; switching doesn't close them.
steps.completionMessage: You're on workspace two. Anything you already had here stays in place.

steps.practicePrompt: Return to the workspace you were just using, with the previous-used-workspace shortcut.
steps.instruction: Press Super, Control, and Tab to return to the workspace you were just using.
steps.detail: This shortcut returns to the last workspace you visited. In this activity, that's workspace one.
steps.completionMessage: And you're back. Now let's move the terminal instead of ourselves.

steps.practicePrompt: Send the practice terminal to workspace two.
steps.note: The terminal moves to workspace two, and you follow it.
steps.instruction: Hold Super and Shift, then press 2 to send this terminal to workspace two.
steps.detail: Super, Shift, and a number moves the focused window to that workspace and follows it there.

help.label: Move it for me
command: local target = assert(hl.get_window("{tutorialWindow}"), "The practice window is unavailable"); hl.dispatch(hl.dsp.focus({ window = "{tutorialWindow}" })); local active = hl.get_active_window(); assert(active and active.address == target.address, "Could not focus the practice window"); hl.dispatch(hl.dsp.window.move({ workspace = "2", window = "{tutorialWindow}" }))

steps.completionMessage: The terminal is now on workspace two, and you've followed it there. Moving a window lets you keep related work together.

steps.practicePrompt: Switch to the next workspace in order.
steps.instruction: Let's hop desktops. Press Super and Tab to move to the next workspace.
steps.detail: Workspaces keep projects separate without minimizing anything. Watch the numbers in the bar.
steps.completionMessage: See the highlight move in the bar? That's you on a new workspace.

steps.practicePrompt: Switch back to the previous workspace in order.
steps.instruction: Now head back. Hold Super and Shift, then press Tab to return to the previous workspace.
steps.detail: Adding Shift reverses the direction. Super plus a number jumps straight to that workspace.
steps.completionMessage: You're back on the previous workspace. Shift reverses the direction of this shortcut.

steps.practicePrompt: Move the practice terminal into the scratchpad, the hidden workspace.
steps.note: The scratchpad is a hidden workspace you can show over your desktop.
steps.instruction: Let's give the scratchpad something useful. Press Super, Alt, and S to put our terminal there.
steps.detail: The scratchpad is a temporary workspace you can reveal over your current one. Your other windows aren't moved.
steps.completionMessage: The terminal is in the scratchpad. Next, reveal it over your current workspace.

steps.practicePrompt: Show the scratchpad so you can see the practice terminal.
steps.instruction: Press Super and S to reveal the scratchpad with your terminal in it.
steps.detail: The scratchpad is a hidden workspace you can show over your current one. Super and S shows or hides it.
steps.completionMessage: There's your terminal, available without leaving this workspace.

steps.practicePrompt: Hide the scratchpad again without closing its terminal.
steps.note: The terminal stays open while the scratchpad is hidden.
steps.instruction: Press Super and S again to tuck the scratchpad away.
steps.detail: Anything you leave in the scratchpad stays there until you call it back.
steps.completionMessage: The scratchpad is hidden, but its terminal is still open. We'll reveal it again before moving the terminal to a numbered workspace.

steps.practicePrompt: Show the scratchpad again and bring the practice terminal into focus.
steps.note: Select our practice terminal if other windows are in the scratchpad.
steps.instruction: Reveal the scratchpad again with Super and S. We'll move the practice terminal only after it has focus.
steps.detail: If the scratchpad contains other windows, select the terminal we opened. The next shortcut moves the focused window, not a window hidden in the scratchpad.
steps.completionMessage: The practice terminal is visible and focused. Now you can move it out of the scratchpad.

steps.practicePrompt: Move the practice terminal out of the scratchpad and onto workspace two.
steps.note: The terminal must be visible and focused before you move it.
steps.instruction: Press Super, Shift, and 2 to bring the practice terminal back to workspace two.
steps.detail: The terminal must be visible and focused. Sending it to a numbered workspace takes it out of the scratchpad.

help.label: Show me how
command: local target = assert(hl.get_window("{tutorialWindow}"), "The practice window is unavailable"); hl.dispatch(hl.dsp.focus({ window = "{tutorialWindow}" })); local active = hl.get_active_window(); assert(active and active.address == target.address, "Could not focus the practice window"); hl.dispatch(hl.dsp.window.move({ window = "{tutorialWindow}", workspace = "2" }))

steps.completionMessage: The terminal is back on workspace two and no longer in the scratchpad.

steps.practicePrompt: Close the practice terminal, leaving your other windows alone.
steps.instruction: Let's leave the desktop tidy. Press Super and W to close our practice terminal.
steps.detail: This closes only the terminal from this lesson. Your other work stays open.
steps.completionMessage: The practice terminal is closed. You've moved between workspaces, moved a window, and used the scratchpad.

references.action: Open the disposable terminal used by this lesson.
Pop a tiled window out, or restore that pop-out to tiling.
references.caution: Start tiled. Pop-out floats, resizes, centers, and pins the window. This lesson uses and restores only its disposable terminal.

references.action: Widen a floating window.
references.caution: Use the physical key immediately left of Backspace. This lesson targets only its disposable terminal.

references.action: Close the focused window.
references.caution: Check focus first. This lesson verifies closure of only its disposable terminal.

wrapUp.text: Nice work. You've practiced opening a disposable terminal, popping it out, resizing it, returning it to tiling, and closing it. Your other windows and workspace settings were left alone.

lessons.title: More window controls
lessons.description: Optional: safely practice pop-out and resizing on a disposable lesson terminal.

steps.practicePrompt: Open the disposable terminal used only by this lesson.
steps.note: Only this newly launched terminal will be changed.
steps.instruction: Press Super and Return to open a disposable practice terminal.
steps.detail: The lesson records the exact new window, so later actions cannot target an app that was already open. Groups combine disposable windows in one tile; Super with a mouse drag moves or resizes. Those and persistent workspace-layout switching remain reference topics because they cannot be verified and restored as reliably as this pop-out practice.

help.label: Launch the practice terminal for me

steps.completionMessage: The disposable terminal is ready. Only this exact window can satisfy the remaining activities.

steps.practicePrompt: Pop the disposable terminal out of the tiled layout.
steps.note: The lesson verifies that its own terminal became floating.
steps.instruction: Press Super and O to pop the practice terminal out. Omarchy floats, centers, resizes, and pins the tiled window.
steps.detail: Pinned pop-outs stay visible across workspaces on this display. You'll resize this same lesson-owned window next, then restore it to tiling before closing it.

help.label: Pop out the practice terminal for me
command: local window = "{tutorialWindow}"; assert(hl.get_window(window), "The practice window is unavailable"); hl.dispatch(hl.dsp.window.float({ action = "enable", window = window })); hl.dispatch(hl.dsp.window.resize({ window = window, x = 1300, y = 900 })); hl.dispatch(hl.dsp.window.center({ window = window })); hl.dispatch(hl.dsp.window.pin({ window = window })); hl.dispatch(hl.dsp.window.alter_zorder({ window = window, mode = "top" })); hl.dispatch(hl.dsp.window.tag({ window = window, tag = "+pop" }))

steps.completionMessage: The disposable terminal is floating. Your other windows were not changed.

steps.practicePrompt: Change the width of the floating disposable terminal.
steps.note: Use the physical key immediately left of Backspace.
steps.instruction: Hold Super and press the key immediately left of Backspace, normally equals, to widen the floating practice terminal.
steps.detail: The lesson compares this owned window's size before and after. Workspace-layout switching is intentionally omitted because it persists user state that cannot always be restored reliably.

help.label: Resize the practice terminal for me
command: hl.dispatch(hl.dsp.window.resize({ window = "{tutorialWindow}", x = 100, y = 0, relative = true }))

steps.completionMessage: The lesson-owned terminal changed width. No existing window was resized.

steps.practicePrompt: Return the disposable pop-out to the tiled layout.
steps.instruction: Press Super and O again to unpin and retile the practice terminal.
steps.detail: This restores the pop-out operation on the same lesson-owned window. It does not change the workspace's saved layout.

help.label: Retile the practice terminal for me
command: local window = "{tutorialWindow}"; assert(hl.get_window(window), "The practice window is unavailable"); hl.dispatch(hl.dsp.window.pin({ window = window })); hl.dispatch(hl.dsp.window.float({ action = "disable", window = window })); hl.dispatch(hl.dsp.window.tag({ window = window, tag = "-pop" }))

steps.completionMessage: The disposable terminal is tiled again.

steps.practicePrompt: Close the disposable terminal opened by this lesson.
steps.instruction: Press Super and W to close the practice terminal.
steps.detail: Completion requires the exact lesson-owned window to close. Existing windows cannot satisfy this activity.

help.label: Close the practice terminal for me

steps.completionMessage: The disposable terminal is closed. Your other windows and settings remain as they were.

references.action: Copy selected text using Omarchy's shared copy shortcut, including in supported terminals.

references.action: Open clipboard history to search recent copies. Use arrow keys to highlight an entry or select with the mouse.

In clipboard history, activate the highlighted entry and attempt immediate paste into the previously focused app.
references.caution: Mouse activation also attempts paste. Behavior depends on the target app; use Shift+Enter for copy-only rather than assuming Enter just copies.

references.action: Select and copy the first sample, then the newer sample. Open history, highlight the first note and use Shift+Enter. Click the destination and paste once; check it matches the first note.

references.action: Compose a smile (😄): tap and release Caps Lock, then press lowercase m, then lowercase s.
references.caution: Separate presses, not held together; no Shift. Caps Lock is Compose by default, but custom mappings may differ.

references.action: Compose a heart (❤️): tap and release Caps Lock, then press lowercase m, then lowercase h.
references.caution: Separate presses, not held together; no Shift. In COURSE practice, enter smile and heart in their respective fields; skip rather than changing custom mappings.

wrapUp.text: Nicely done. You've explored clipboard history and practiced Compose sequences. A few useful characters and shortcuts can save you time.

lessons.title: Clipboard and Compose
lessons.description: Retrieve older clipboard entries and type emojis with sequential Compose keys.

steps.instruction: Omarchy provides shared copy and paste shortcuts: Super and C to copy, and Super and V to paste. They work across supported apps, including the terminal, where the usual shortcuts can differ.
steps.detail: Select text before copying, then choose where to paste it. Custom bindings and individual apps can affect these shortcuts.

steps.practicePrompt: Open clipboard history to see where earlier copied items are kept.
steps.note: History may contain private information; select entries carefully.
steps.instruction: Copied something earlier? Hold Super and Control, then press V to open your clipboard history.
steps.detail: Clipboard history keeps recent copied items. Activating an entry normally pastes it into the previously focused field. Shift+Enter copies an entry without pasting. To cancel, Escape clears typed text; press it again to close, or once if empty. Be mindful of private information in your history.
steps.completionMessage: Clipboard history is open. After releasing the keys, select an entry and use Shift and Enter to copy it without pasting. Regular Enter pastes into the previous field.

steps.note: This exercise replaces your clipboard with harmless sample text.
steps.instruction: Let's make clipboard history useful. Copy two sample notes. Find the older one in history, use Shift and Enter to copy it without pasting, then paste it into the exercise.
steps.detail: The exercise uses harmless text, but it replaces the current clipboard. Keys go to the exercise window until you finish or close it.
steps.completionMessage: You retrieved an older clipboard entry and pasted it. That's useful when a newer copy replaces something you still need.

steps.instruction: Omarchy uses Caps Lock as the Compose key by default, instead of toggling capital letters. Tap and release Caps Lock, then m, then s for a smile. These are separate presses, not a shortcut you hold together.
steps.detail: Compose uses separate key presses, not keys held together. Use lowercase letters without Shift. We'll practice a smile and a heart next. Custom keyboard settings may use a different Compose key.

steps.note: Custom Compose settings may differ; skipping is fine.
steps.instruction: Let's type a smile and a heart without opening the emoji picker. Follow the keys in order, one at a time.
steps.detail: The normal text field receives Compose input. The exercise checks the resulting emojis. If Caps Lock has been remapped, use the picker in everyday work and skip this exercise rather than changing your keyboard settings.
steps.completionMessage: Two little sequences, two emojis. That's Compose: tap the keys in order, instead of holding a chord.

references.action: Open Capture for screenshots, recordings, color picking and text extraction. Use the menu if your keyboard has no Print key.
Start a screenshot with the frozen-screen picker; drag over the desired region. Alternatively search Screenshot in the Omarchy menu.
references.caution: Inspect for private content first. Screenshots save to the configured Pictures directory and clipboard.

references.action: In the screenshot picker, use Tab to select a window, then Enter to capture the selected window.
references.caution: These are sequential presses in the picker, not a held chord. Check the selected window before capturing.

references.action: In the screenshot picker, capture the focused monitor.
references.caution: Includes visible private windows and notifications on that monitor; inspect before capturing.

references.action: Cancel screenshot region selection without taking a capture.
Click the screenshot notification to open the captured image for editing.
references.caution: Verify it is the intended screenshot notification before invoking its action.

references.action: Invoke the latest notification's action; when it is the screenshot notification, open the screenshot editor.

references.action: Select only the harmless card, inspect the saved image, copy its file path and add a label to the preview.

references.action: Open recording options, or stop an active recording. Choices: no audio; desktop audio; desktop + microphone audio; or desktop + microphone audio + webcam when available. Saved clips go to the configured Videos directory.
references.caution: Microphone includes desktop audio; webcam includes both. Review the region and recording indicator, know how to stop, and get permission before recording other people's voices or private content.

references.action: Select and review the animated card's region. Explicitly start a silent recording, record at least one second, stop your recording, then play the saved clip.
references.caution: This course-specific recorder uses no microphone or webcam and owns only its recording; it does not stop an existing recorder. This is separate from native recording options.

references.action: Extract text from a selected screen region with OCR (optical character recognition).
references.caution: Recognition can make mistakes. Proofread against the source before using the text; avoid private regions.

references.action: Select the sample text card, extract it, copy the recognized sample and paste it into the destination. Compare every word with the original.
references.caution: Requires slurp, grim and tesseract; course verification is a reviewed sample, not a guarantee of general OCR accuracy.

references.action: Search QR Code to select and decode a code already on screen, then inspect the decoded text.
references.caution: Decoding is not permission to open an unknown link.

references.action: Prepare the harmless QR sample, select and decode it, copy the result and paste it below to compare with the sample.
references.caution: The sample contains text, not a website; no link is opened. Requires qrencode, slurp, grim and zbarimg.

wrapUp.text: That wraps up capture. You've practiced making a screenshot and a short recording. Remember to check for private information before sharing.

lessons.title: Capture
lessons.description: Capture an image, record and replay a short clip, and optionally extract text or decode a QR code.

steps.practicePrompt: Open the Capture menu without starting a capture.
steps.instruction: Grab what's on screen. Hold Super and Control, then press C to open the Capture menu.
steps.detail: Screenshots, screen recordings, color picking, and text extraction all start here.
steps.completionMessage: Screenshots, recordings, and more, all from one menu.

steps.instruction: To take a screenshot, press Print. No Print key? Search Screenshot in the Omarchy menu instead. Drag over the area you want to capture. Escape cancels.
steps.detail: The native picker freezes the screen. Tab selects a window and Enter captures it; Control+Enter captures the focused monitor, not the entire multi-monitor desktop. Screenshots save to your configured Pictures directory and clipboard. Click the screenshot notification to edit it, or use Super+Alt+Comma while it's the latest actionable notification. Avoid private content before capturing.

steps.note: Capture only the sample card, not private windows or notifications.
steps.instruction: Capture the practice card, inspect the saved image, copy its file path, and add a label to the preview.
steps.detail: Only capture the sample card, not private windows or notifications. The exercise uses its own capture tools. Preview labels don't alter the saved image, and nothing is uploaded.
steps.completionMessage: You've captured and reviewed an image, copied its path, and labeled the preview. The saved image itself is unchanged.

steps.instruction: Alt and Print opens recording choices, or stops a recording that's already running. Without a Print key, use the Capture menu. Microphone includes desktop audio; webcam includes both. Keep private content and other people's voices out. Watch the recording indicator, and know how to stop before starting.
steps.detail: The choices are "With no audio", "With desktop audio", "With desktop + microphone audio", and, when a webcam is available, "With desktop + microphone audio + webcam". Native recordings go to your configured Videos directory. Never include someone else's voice, private windows, or notifications without permission. Our practice recording is silent and limited to a region you choose.
steps.note: Webcam includes desktop and microphone audio; our practice recording is silent.
Review the selected region; no microphone or webcam is enabled.
steps.instruction: Let's make a short, silent recording of the practice card. Start explicitly, stop it yourself, then play the saved clip.
steps.detail: No microphone or webcam is enabled. The exercise owns only its recorder and output. It must not stop an existing recording. Review the selected region before starting.
steps.completionMessage: You started, stopped, and replayed a real recording. Knowing how to stop is just as important as knowing how to start.

steps.note: OCR turns images into text; check the result for mistakes.
steps.instruction: An image can contain useful text. Select the sample text on the practice card, extract it, and paste the result.
steps.detail: OCR means optical character recognition. Super+Ctrl+Print opens text capture. Recognition can make mistakes, so compare the pasted words with the original. This optional exercise uses only a harmless sample.
steps.completionMessage: You turned pixels into editable text. Give extracted text a quick proofread before you use it.

steps.note: Our sample contains harmless text; no website will open.

references.action: Open the Omarchy menu, search Install and press Enter. Prefer official packages; review community Arch User Repository (AUR) packages more closely.

references.action: Open the Omarchy menu, search Remove and press Enter. Uninstall only after checking the package name and full dependency list.
references.caution: Removal may affect other software. Cancel if you do not understand the proposed changes.

references.action: Open the Omarchy menu, search Defaults and press Enter to see which installed apps Omarchy launches by default.
references.caution: Default changes affect future launches immediately. Installing an app and making it the default are separate decisions.

references.action: Open the Omarchy menu, search Update and press Enter. Save work, review proposed changes and use the stable channel for everyday updates.
references.caution: Some installations create rollback snapshots before updates. Snapshots are not independent backups of personal files.

references.action: Open the Omarchy menu, search Hardware and choose the result under Update to inspect targeted hardware restarts.
references.caution: Network or audio restarts can interrupt calls, downloads and recordings. Back up custom settings under ~/.config before resets; do not edit packaged defaults under /usr/share/omarchy.

lessons.title: Apps and upkeep
lessons.description: Find install, removal, defaults, updates, and recovery tools without changing the system.

steps.practicePrompt: Open Install from the Omarchy menu. Look only; don't select an installation type.
steps.instruction: Press Super and Space, type Install, then press Enter. Look at the available installation types, but don't install anything. Prefer official packages; community packages from the Arch User Repository, or AUR, need closer review.
steps.detail: Opening Install is safe. Choosing an installation type can continue into a workflow that requests your password and changes the system, so stop at this menu. Press Escape until the menu closes to finish.
steps.note: Look only: don't select an installation type.
steps.completionMessage: You inspected Install and closed the menu without changing the system.

steps.practicePrompt: Open Remove from the Omarchy menu. Look only; don't select anything to remove.
steps.instruction: Press Super and Space, type Remove, then press Enter. Look at the removal categories, but don't select one. Before uninstalling software, check its name and every dependency the removal would affect.
steps.detail: A dependency is software another app needs. Opening Remove is safe; choosing an item can begin an uninstall workflow, so stop at this menu. Press Escape until the menu closes to finish.
steps.note: Look only: don't select anything to remove.
steps.completionMessage: You inspected Remove and closed the menu without uninstalling anything.

steps.practicePrompt: Open Defaults from the Omarchy menu. Look only; keep your current defaults.
steps.instruction: Press Super and Space, type Defaults, then press Enter. Look at the kinds of default apps you can choose, but don't change one. Installing an app and making it the default are separate decisions.
steps.detail: Selecting a default changes future launches immediately. Keep your current settings. Press Escape until the menu closes to finish.
steps.note: Look only: selecting a default changes future launches.
steps.completionMessage: You inspected Defaults and closed the menu without changing your settings.

steps.practicePrompt: Open Update from the Omarchy menu. Look only; don't run an update or change channels.
steps.instruction: Press Super and Space, type Update, then press Enter. Look at the available update tools, but don't select one. Before a real update, save your work, review the changes, and use the stable channel for everyday use.
steps.detail: Some installations create filesystem snapshots before updates, but a snapshot isn't an independent backup of your personal files. Opening this menu doesn't run an update. Press Escape until the menu closes to finish.
steps.note: Look only: don't run an update or change channels.
steps.completionMessage: You inspected Update and closed the menu without running an update.

steps.practicePrompt: Open Update, Hardware. Look only; don't restart any hardware service.
steps.instruction: Press Super and Space, type Hardware, then choose the result under Update. Look at the targeted restarts, but don't select one. A restart can interrupt calls, downloads, or recordings.
steps.detail: Use Update, Hardware when a specific device service stops working. Resetting configuration is different and can replace settings under ~/.config; don't edit packaged defaults under /usr/share/omarchy. Press Escape until the menu closes to finish.
steps.note: Choose Hardware under Update, then look only; don't restart a service.
steps.completionMessage: You inspected Update, Hardware and closed the menu without restarting a service.

references.action: Open Trigger > Hardware for available laptop display, mirror, GPU, touchpad, haptics and touchscreen actions.
references.caution: Selecting an action can change device behavior immediately. Keyboard settings are under Setup > Input or Keybindings; audio, Bluetooth and display have separate panels.

references.action: Open Display for text size, scale, supported brightness and multi-display enable/disable controls. Escape closes the panel.
references.caution: Changes apply immediately. Configure resolution separately under Setup > Monitors.

references.action: Open System for lock, suspend, logout, reboot and shutdown.
references.caution: Inspect without selecting a disruptive action; save work before logging out, restarting or shutting down.

references.action: Lock the screen without suspending the computer.
references.caution: Optional practice: save work and know your password before locking. You need it to return.

references.action: When ready, explicitly choose the lock button, unlock with your password, then return to the course. Skip if you are not ready.
references.caution: Opening the exercise alone does not lock the computer.

wrapUp.text: That wraps up setup and system controls. You know where to look when you need them, without changing settings just for practice.

lessons.title: Setup and system
lessons.description: Reach hardware setup, display settings, and safe system actions from the keyboard.

steps.practicePrompt: Open the Hardware menu. Look only: selecting an action can change device behavior immediately.
steps.instruction: Hold Super and Control, then press H to open the Hardware menu. Opening it is safe, but selecting an action can change device behavior immediately. Just look for this lesson; don't select an action.
steps.detail: This is Trigger > Hardware. Depending on your hardware, it offers Laptop Display, Mirror Display, Hybrid GPU, Touchpad, Touchpad Haptics, and Touchscreen controls. Audio, Bluetooth, and Display have separate panels. Keyboard configuration is under Setup > Input or Setup > Keybindings.
steps.note: Look only: selecting a hardware action can change device behavior immediately.
steps.completionMessage: You're in Trigger, Hardware. Install and Update sit alongside Trigger at the root of the Omarchy menu, not inside Hardware.

steps.practicePrompt: Open the Display panel. Leave its controls unchanged; changes apply immediately.
steps.note: Display changes apply immediately; leave the controls unchanged.
steps.instruction: Hold Super and Control, then press D to open the Display panel. Just look for now: changes apply immediately, so leave the controls unchanged.
steps.detail: The panel offers text size and scale, brightness where supported, and display enable/disable controls when multiple displays are available. Resolution is configured separately under Setup > Monitors.
steps.completionMessage: The Display panel is open. Text size and scale are here, with brightness and display switches where available. These controls apply immediately, so looking is enough for this lesson.

steps.practicePrompt: Open the System menu. Don't select Lock, Logout, Restart, or Shutdown.
steps.note: Close the menu without choosing logout, restart, or shutdown.
steps.instruction: Hold Super and press Escape to open the System menu.
steps.detail: Lock, suspend, log out, reboot, or shut down from one keyboard-driven list.
steps.completionMessage: The System menu is open. Close it without selecting an action to keep working; actions such as logout or shutdown can interrupt your session.

steps.note: Locking is optional; save your work and know your password first.
steps.instruction: Build one useful habit: Super, Control, and L locks your screen. Practice only when you're ready.

steps.completionMessage: You've locked the computer and returned after unlocking it. Use that shortcut when you step away.

references.action: Open the emoji picker, type a search word and press Enter to insert the selection into the previously focused text field.
references.caution: Check the intended destination before choosing an emoji.

references.caution: Before scheduling, Escape clears typed text; press again to close, or once if empty.

references.caution: Review the resulting text; do not leave recording active. The toggle shortcut is an alternative if your keyboard lacks F9.

references.action: Check availability, enable the practice field when ready, use the dictation shortcut for 'Omarchy practice', stop and review the words.
references.caution: The exercise does not start your microphone. It checks the entered sample and your review, not whether speech produced the text.

references.action: Inspect whether the Voxtype config documents replacements, then apply a specific correction to a harmless simulated transcript.
references.caution: The course reads only replacement metadata and never displays or edits the real config. A bundled sample is used when Voxtype or its config is unavailable.

wrapUp.text: That wraps up productivity extras. You've explored emojis, reminders, and dictation. Choose the tools that help with your own work.

lessons.title: Productivity extras
lessons.description: Optional: the emoji picker, reminders, local dictation, and word corrections.

steps.practicePrompt: Open the activity monitor to inspect resource use. Don't stop any programs.
steps.note: Inspect resource use without stopping any programs.
steps.instruction: Wondering what's using your computer? Press Super, Control, and T to open the activity monitor.
steps.detail: The activity monitor shows processor use, memory, storage, and running programs. Don't stop any programs for this lesson.
steps.completionMessage: The activity monitor is open. Use it to understand resource use before deciding whether anything needs attention.

steps.practicePrompt: Close the activity-monitor window opened by this lesson.
steps.instruction: Press Super and W to close our activity monitor.
steps.detail: This closes only the activity monitor opened here. Existing tool windows stay open.

steps.note: The lesson checks that the calculator opens, not your calculation.

steps.detail: The calculator accepts expressions such as 5 + 5. This activity only asks you to open it, and an existing calculator window won't be closed.
steps.completionMessage: The calculator is open and ready whenever you need a quick calculation.

steps.practicePrompt: Close the calculator opened by this lesson.
steps.instruction: Press Super and W to close our calculator.
steps.detail: This closes only the calculator opened here. Existing calculator windows stay open.

steps.practicePrompt: Open Disk Usage and inspect folder sizes without deleting anything.
steps.instruction: Choose Open Disk Usage, wait for the scan, then navigate the dua list to inspect which top-level folders use space.

steps.note: Read-only exploration: do not delete or mark entries for removal.
steps.completionMessage: Disk Usage is scanning in a lesson-owned terminal. Inspect sizes and navigate folders; do not delete anything.

keys: Install > Web App / Remove > Web App
references.action: Install Web App asks for a name and website URL to create a launcher. Remove Web App removes that launcher, not your website account.

references.action: Explicitly create the isolated demo entry, open its local preview, then remove it.
references.caution: This is not an installed app: it only uses the exercise folder, does not change Apps, and the local preview makes no network request.

references.action: Convert a separate media copy at a sensible resolution. Compare file size and playback quality before sharing. MP4 suits longer clips; GIF suits short silent loops.
references.caution: Keep the original. Neither format nor conversion guarantees a smaller file; GIF can be larger than MP4.

references.action: Generate the harmless silent sample, play the original, choose a lower resolution and create a separate MP4 copy. Play the output and compare size and quality.
references.caution: Requires ffmpeg and ffprobe. The course keeps the original; evaluate output rather than assuming lower resolution always means acceptable quality.

references.action: Open Share; opening the menu alone sends nothing.
references.caution: Verify content and recipient before sending. Escape clears typed text; press again to close, or once if empty.

references.action: For a real transfer, use LocalSend on both devices with a network connection between them. Inspect the file and verify the intended recipient before sending; confirm receipt.
references.caution: Never send private files or secrets merely to test sharing. A nearby device is not necessarily the intended recipient.

references.action: Prepare and read the sample file, choose 'My test phone (demo)', then confirm you checked the file and demo recipient.

lessons.title: Create and share
lessons.description: Optional: web-app launchers, smaller video files, and safe LocalSend preparation.

steps.note: This local demo doesn't change your Apps menu.
steps.instruction: A web app gives a website its own launcher. Create a local demo entry, preview it, then remove it. This practice doesn't add anything to your Apps menu.
steps.detail: In everyday Omarchy, Install Web App asks for a name and website address; Remove Web App removes its launcher. This exercise uses a temporary local preview and makes no network request.
steps.completionMessage: A web app is a launcher for a site, not a separate account or a replacement for the browser's security.

steps.note: Transcoding converts media; your original file is kept.
steps.instruction: A recording can be too large to share comfortably. Let's create a smaller copy of a harmless practice clip and inspect the result.
steps.detail: Transcoding means converting media. Keep the original, choose a sensible resolution, and compare the output before sharing. MP4 suits longer clips; GIF can be convenient for short, silent loops but isn't always smaller.
steps.completionMessage: You've created a separate output and kept the original. Check quality and size before you share it.

steps.practicePrompt: Open the Share menu without starting a transfer.
steps.note: Opening the menu sends nothing; check the file and recipient before sharing.
steps.instruction: Here's an optional tool for sharing. Press Super, Control, and S to open the Share menu.
steps.detail: Opening the menu sends nothing. Before sharing, check the selected content and recipient. Never send secrets or personal files just to complete a lesson. Escape clears typed text; press it again to close, or once if empty.
steps.completionMessage: The Share menu is open. Sending anything is optional and always your decision.

steps.note: This rehearsal doesn't discover devices or send anything.
steps.instruction: LocalSend shares files with nearby devices. In this rehearsal, review a sample file and choose an intended demo recipient. Nothing will be sent.
steps.detail: Real transfers need LocalSend on both devices and a network connection between them. Check both the file and recipient before sending. This exercise doesn't discover devices or confirm delivery.
steps.completionMessage: You reviewed the safe sharing workflow. Delivery to another device is a separate action that this course doesn't assume.
